prompt: What is the period of $y = \tan(3\theta)$, in degrees?
hint: Start from the period of plain tangent — and it is NOT $360^\circ$.

hints.text: Start from the period of plain tangent — and it is NOT $360^\circ$.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm up with $y = \tan(2\theta)$: start from the tangent period $180^\circ$ and divide by $2$ to get $90^\circ$. Same recipe, just with $3$ instead of $2$.
$y = \tan\theta$ has period $180^\circ$; a coefficient $B$ inside divides that period by $B$.

explanation: The period of $y = \tan\theta$ is $180^\circ$, half that of sine and cosine.

alternativeExplanations.title: Track the asymptotes
steps: The next one is at $3\theta = 270^\circ$, so $\theta = 90^\circ$.
Consecutive asymptotes are $60^\circ$ apart, and one full branch fits between them — the period is $60^\circ$.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ The trap here
steps: The trap is answering $120^\circ$ by computing $\frac{360^\circ}{3}$ out of habit.
That formula belongs to sine and cosine. Tangent starts from $180^\circ$, not $360^\circ$.
Before dividing by $B$, always ask which function you are in: sine and cosine start at $360^\circ$, tangent and cotangent start at $180^\circ$.
